chapter: Early bands and Luis Russell's Harlem
title: Joining Luis Russell: Savoy, Apollo and the band's people
summary: He recalls the singer Lee Richardson, trombonist Emery Thompson and his own drum feature.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So you say, okay, I’m going to go head into this gig with Luis Russell. So what happened when you showed up for the gig?

The thing about it, I had a feeling to want to play with a big band right after, and that thing came right on time, to go to New York. I started at the Savoy Ballroom with him, and the Apollo Theater, and all those places.
Who else was in the band?

Oh boy. There were some older guys in the band. They always had a singer – a male singer. There was one saxophonist, played tenor, from Harlem: Ed [?] – he didn’t continue on. He was good. Then they started getting some younger players in the band. They got a younger trombone player from New Orleans, who’s still playing. His hair is white now. He’s younger than I am. Emery Thompson, his name is. He was with the band. He wasn’t there when I joined, but I think he come in while I was there. They had a singer by the name of Lee Richardson that was making – had hit records. I had stayed with the band one year, I quit, and then I went back when Lee had these records coming out. Once we played the Earl Theater in Philadelphia. Nat Cole was headlining, but Lee Richardson was kicking butt. All them little girls – all the girls would come. I had a feature drum thing with the band. So it was very exciting, playing all those theaters and dances.
